item.title: The Uncanny Valley and the Rising Power of Anti-AI Sentiment
item.description:
📝 People encounter text that sounds conversational, voices that sound natural, images and video that almost pass, and agents that mimic competence, memory, initiative, or empathy. Repeated contact gives that shift its force. AI often presents the kind of near-human abnormality that could fit that account.

item.title: 2,100 Swiss municipalities showing which provider handles their official email
item.description:
📝 A map of all ~2,100 Swiss municipalities showing which provider handles their official email — grouped by jurisdiction — based on public DNS records and other public network signals. This map makes the current provider landscape visible. Disclaimer: DNS records indicate mail routing and authorized senders, not necessarily where data is stored.
🔗 Read more: https://mxmap.ch/

item.title: Scientific datasets are riddled with copy-paste errors
item.description:
📝 The above data comes from a landmark paper in Parkinson's Disease research, which provided the first-ever evidence that the disease originates in the gut rather than the brain. But the underlying data contains sequences of duplicated values that should belong to completely different individual mice. Both cases had publicly available datasets with entire blocks of copy-pasted data that seemed quite trivial to detect.
🔗 Read more: https://www.sciencedetective.org/scientific-datasets-are-riddled-with-copy-paste-errors/

item.title: Got an Old Kindle? It Might Not Work Anymore
item.description:
📝 Why Amazon is ending support for older KindlesIf you own one of the following Kindles, you won’t be able to download new books after May 20: Kindle 1st Generation (2007), Kindle DX (2009), Kindle DX Graphite (2010), Kindle Keyboard (2010), Kindle 4 (2011), Kindle Touch (2011), Kindle 5 (2012), and the Kindle Paperwhite 1st Generation (2012). The Fire tablets that will no longer be supported are: Kindle Fire 1st Generation (2011), Kindle Fire 2nd Generation (2012), Kindle Fire HD 7 (2012), and Kindle Fire HD 8. Amazon says this will impact less than 3% of its Kindle e-reader and Kindle Fire customers worldwide.
🔗 Read more: https://www.nytimes.com/wirecutter/reviews/older-kindle-support-ending/
